items.title: Evaluate Department Consolidations
items.officialTitle: A RESOLUTION OF THE MAYOR AND CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF MIAMI BEACH, FLORIDA, DIRECTING THE CITY ADMINISTRATION TO EVALUATE THE POTENTIAL CONSOLIDATION AND/OR SHARING OF STAFF AND ADMINISTRATIVE RESOURCES BETWEEN THE TRANSPORTATION AND MOBILITY DEPARTMENT AND THE PARKING DEPARTMENT, AND BETWEEN THE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT AND THE TOURISM AND CULTURE DEPARTMENT; TO IDENTIFY ANY OTHER DEPARTMENTAL CONSOLIDATIONS, COMMON-MANAGEMENT STRUCTURES, OR SHARED-SERVICE OPPORTUNITIES THE ADMINISTRATION DEEMS APPROPRIATE; AND TO PRESENT ITS FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS TO THE MAYOR AND CITY COMMISSION AT THE OCTOBER 14, 2026 CITY COMMISSION MEETING, WITH THE PRIMARY GOALS OF REDUCING RECURRING PERSONNEL AND OPERATING COSTS, ELIMINATING DUPLICATIVE FUNCTIONS, IMPROVING COORDINATION AND SERVICE DELIVERY, AND INCREASING GOVERNMENT EFFICIENCY.

items.title: Enhance Police Oversight Transparency
items.officialTitle: A RESOLUTION OF THE MAYOR AND CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF MIAMI BEACH, FLORIDA, ESTABLISHING ENHANCED TRANSPARENCY AND INDEPENDENT OVERSIGHT OF COMPLETED MIAMI BEACH POLICE DEPARTMENT INTERNAL AFFAIRS INVESTIGATIONS BY REQUIRING COMMISSION NOTIFICATION OF SUBSTANTIATED MISCONDUCT AND TRANSMISSION OF COMPLETED INTERNAL AFFAIRS INVESTIGATIVE FILES TO THE OFFICE OF INSPECTOR GENERAL; AND RECOGNIZING AND AFFIRMING THE AUTHORITY OF THE OFFICE OF INSPECTOR GENERAL, IN ITS SOLE AND INDEPENDENT DISCRETION, TO AUDIT OR REVIEW THE MIAMI BEACH POLICE DEPARTMENT’S ADMINISTRATION, OPERATION, AND INSTITUTIONAL HANDLING OF COMPLETED INTERNAL AFFAIRS MATTERS WITHIN THE SCOPE OF THE CITY CHARTER AND ITS LEGAL AUTHORITY.

items.title: File FDLE Misconduct Complaint
items.officialTitle: A RESOLUTION OF THE MAYOR AND CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF MIAMI BEACH, FLORIDA, (1) DIRECTING THE CITY ADMINISTRATION TO PREPARE AND TRANSMIT TO THE FLORIDA DEPARTMENT OF LAW ENFORCEMENT (“FDLE”), PROFESSIONAL COMPLIANCE SECTION, A SIGNED, VERIFIABLE COMPLAINT, ON BEHALF OF THE CITY OF MIAMI BEACH, CONTAINING SPECIFIC ALLEGATIONS OF POTENTIAL NONCOMPLIANCE BY THE INDIVIDUAL OFFICERS WITH SECTION 943.13(7), FLORIDA STATUTES, AND REQUESTING INDEPENDENT REVIEW, AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE SUCH COMPLAINT ON BEHALF OF THE CITY; (2) DIRECTING THE CITY ADMINISTRATION TO TRANSMIT THE COMPLETE INVESTIGATIVE FILE, EVIDENCE, FINDINGS, AND ALL SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION AND RECORDS RELATING TO MIAMI BEACH POLICE DEPARTMENT INTERNAL AFFAIRS CASE NO. I2023-007 TO FDLE, CRIMINAL JUSTICE PROFESSIONALISM PROGRAM, FOR THEIR INDEPENDENT REVIEW AND DETERMINATION OF WHETHER THE CONDUCT IDENTIFIED THEREIN CONSTITUTES A FAILURE TO MAINTAIN THE GOOD MORAL CHARACTER REQUIRED OF CERTIFIED LAW-ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS UNDER SECTION 943.13(7), FLORIDA STATUTES, AND APPLICABLE RULES OF THE CRIMINAL JUSTICE STANDARDS AND TRAINING COMMISSION (“CJSTC”); (3) REQUESTING THAT FDLE AND CJSTC INDEPENDENTLY REVIEW, IN ADDITION TO THE INDIVIDUAL OFFICERS’ CONDUCT, WHETHER MBPD COMPLIED WITH ITS INVESTIGATION, DISPOSITION, AND REPORTING OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 943.1395(5), FLORIDA STATUTES, AND APPLICABLE COMMISSION RULES, AND WHETHER ANY FURTHER INVESTIGATION OR CERTIFICATION ACTION IS WARRANTED; (4) DIRECTING THAT ANY CONFIDENTIAL OR RESTRICTED MATERIALS BE TRANSMITTED ONLY THROUGH APPROPRIATE SECURE LAW-ENFORCEMENT CHANNELS; AND (5) DIRECTING THE CITY CLERK TO TRANSMIT A CERTIFIED COPY OF THIS RESOLUTION TO THE FLORIDA DEPARTMENT OF LAW ENFORCEMENT, PROFESSIONAL COMPLIANCE SECTION, AND THE CRIMINAL JUSTICE STANDARDS AND TRAINING COMMISSION.

items.title: Moratorium on LPR Deployments
items.officialTitle: A RESOLUTION OF THE MAYOR AND CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF MIAMI BEACH, FLORIDA, IMPOSING A MORATORIUM ON NEW AND EXPANDED AUTOMATED LICENSE PLATE READER (“LPR”) DEPLOYMENTS, PURCHASES, PROCUREMENTS, CONTRACTS, AND DATA-SHARING ARRANGEMENTS PENDING A COMPREHENSIVE 90-DAY REVIEW AND SUBSEQUENT AFFIRMATIVE APPROVAL OF THE MAYOR AND CITY COMMISSION; ESTABLISHING INTERIM SAFEGUARDS GOVERNING THE CITY’S CONTINUED USE OF EXISTING LPR SYSTEMS AND DATABASES; DIRECTING THE CITY ADMINISTRATION, AND REQUESTING THE ASSISTANCE AND PARTICIPATION OF THE OFFICE OF THE CITY ATTORNEY AND, CONSISTENT WITH ITS INDEPENDENT AUTHORITY, THE OFFICE OF THE INSPECTOR GENERAL, TO CONDUCT A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF THE CITY’S USE OF LPR TECHNOLOGY, INCLUDING PRIVACY AND CONSTITUTIONAL CONCERNS, DATA RETENTION, THIRD-PARTY VENDOR ACCESS, INTERAGENCY DATA SHARING, AUDITING, CYBERSECURITY, AND EXISTING CONTRACTUAL ARRANGEMENTS; DIRECTING THAT THE FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS OF SUCH REVIEW BE REPORTED TO THE MAYOR AND CITY COMMISSION WITHIN 90 DAYS; PROVIDING THAT, FOLLOWING RECEIPT, THE MAYOR AND CITY COMMISSION SHALL REVIEW AND DISCUSS THE FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS AND DETERMINE WHETHER THE CITY’S EXISTING LPR PROGRAM SHOULD CONTINUE, CONTINUE SUBJECT TO ADDITIONAL OR MODIFIED SAFEGUARDS OR RESTRICTIONS, OR BE SUSPENDED; AND PROVIDING THAT THE MORATORIUM SHALL REMAIN IN EFFECT UNLESS AND UNTIL NEW OR EXPANDED LPR ACTIVITY IS AFFIRMATIVELY AUTHORIZED BY THE MAYOR AND CITY COMMISSION.
